newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway debt dips on CPI but recovers, crown down.
newsitem.headline: Norway debt dips on CPI but recovers, crown down.

text.p: 1400 GMT -- Norwegian debt weakened after higher than forecast headline inflation figures and the yield spread in 10-year sector with German Bunds widened.
Crown lost ground and dealers saw no clear reason. Firmer mark, weaker oil prices and nervousness after CPI data could all be impacting currency, they said.
* 2007 bond yield one basis point higher at 5.96 pct
* Norway over Bunds gap one point wider at 17 basis points
* Three-month eurokrone three basis points higher at 3.45 pct
* Crown 102.13 vs inverse European Currency Unit index vs 101.83
Norwegian bond yields rose slightly as May inflation data came in higher than expected and the yield spread with German widened.
But long yields later recovered slightly to close just one basis point higher at 5.96 percent.
May's CPI rose 2.7 percent year-on-year and was up 0.3 percent from April. Government department Statistics Norway attributed the increase to higher prices for gasoline and foodstuffs.
An average forecast by 10 economists polled by Reuters estimated the year-on-year rise at 2.47 percent and a month-on-month increase of 0.1 percent.
"There was a discrepancy between the headline inflation figure and expectations because I think many people failed to recognise that the gasoline price war had ended," said one analyst.
"But the underlying inflation figure, which I make unchanged from April at 1.6 percent, was better than expected. I see no serious impact from these figures."
The Norwegian crown weakened to an intraday low at around 4.1820 against the mark -- the lowest level since May 26 -- and players said there was no clear cut cause.
"Maybe people got a bit nervous when they initially saw the inflation figure, or maybe it's because the oil price has fallen significantly," said a London-based analyst.
"But the mark has been much better bid against a series of European currencies, that's the more likely explanation," he said.
